doc.title: Howard Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019

title: Archie Shepp, Coltrane and 'angry' music
summary: Asked whether progressive music was angry, he says Archie was aggressive but Coltrane was beautiful and delicate.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: That’s a great — that’s some drama there, boy, that is jazz drama. I can just picture it, and the audience, like okay what’s Mingus going to do next, and how’s this young man going to respond. That’s a really cool story. Wow. Just, and a long line, of I was trying to think of people who you haven’t played with, and that’s sort of hard. But you seemed to enter the jazz world with pretty progressive music, right? You played with Archie Shepp and some people say that much of that music sounds angry.
Yeah, what do you think about that?

Yeah. About Archie’s especially because he was very aggressive. Well they called Coltrane angry. So much beauty in Coltrane, you know, whether it’s fast or slow. It’s almost delicate to me, you know, the loudest Coltrane stuff you can find seems delicate.
